competitors.name: IBEAMS (IBEUK)
competitors.what_they_offer: Cloud management system for maktabs, madrasahs and Islamic private schools covering attendance, fees (outstanding balances, reminders), a parent portal showing attendance, invoices and communications, and student records.
competitors.pricing: Published in GBP per month: Basic £15 (up to 50 students), Standard £30 (up to 150), Enterprise £60 (unlimited); unlimited teachers, email support, no set-up fee. Add-ons include Student Diary £10/month, phone & Telegram support £10/month, remove ads £5/month.
competitors.overlap: Madrasah side: registers/attendance, fees, parent access.
competitors.gap_vs_masjidone: Prayer times, congregation app, masjid website, hall screens and donations are not mentioned on the pages fetched. Phone support is a paid add-on (£10/month) per its pricing page.

competitors.name: Teach 'n Go
competitors.what_they_offer: General class-management platform with an Islamic school/Qur'an programme page: per-session attendance, invoices/receipts and fee tracking, a parent and learner portal, recurring evening/weekend scheduling, announcements, mobile app, 24 languages including Arabic.
competitors.overlap: Madrasah side: registers, fees, parent access, family communications.
competitors.gap_vs_masjidone: Prayer times, donations and mosque/congregation apps are not mentioned on the page fetched; it is a general education tool rather than masjid-specific. Pricing not shown on that page (14-day free trial advertised).

competitors.name: Masjidbox
competitors.what_they_offer: Suite of mosque products: Screens (digital signage with prayer times, countdown, announcements, donation campaigns), branded Applications, web Pages with custom domain, Donations, widgets, social visuals and calendars, plus a worshipper app (Masjidbox One).
competitors.pricing: Published in EUR per month: Screens Free €0 / Silver €29; Applications Free €0 / Silver €29; Pages Free €0 / Silver €15; Global plan (all three) €62. Donations listed as free with a '0% platform fee' (Stripe/bank transfer fees may apply). Annual billing advertised as '1 month free'.
competitors.overlap: Congregation side almost entirely: prayer-time screens, congregation app, website on own domain, donations with 0% platform fee, UK Gift Aid (monthly reports; changelog dated 3 June 2026 says automatic HMRC Gift Aid claiming is live for eligible UK mosques).
competitors.gap_vs_masjidone: Madrasah management (registers, fees, parent access, one family record) is not mentioned on the pages fetched. UK presence beyond UK customers/Gift Aid is not stated; pricing is in EUR.

competitors.name: MosqueApp Ltd
competitors.what_they_offer: UK company (High Wycombe) building custom-branded iOS/Android apps for mosques with prayer times, Adhan and push notifications, donations (Sadaqah, Zakat, appeals) and live streaming; also offers app-synced display screens and mosque websites.
competitors.pricing: Figures not published. Site states no subscription fees: a one-off build cost plus a small annual hosting and maintenance fee; quote/demo required.
competitors.overlap: Congregation app, prayer times, notices/notifications, donations, display screens, website; UK-based team.
competitors.gap_vs_masjidone: A 'Madrassa Module' is described as a future feature, so madrasah registers, fees and parent access are not available per the page fetched. Gift Aid and commission terms not mentioned on the page fetched.

competitors.name: MAWAQIT
competitors.what_they_offer: Non-profit, open-source prayer-time platform; its app lists mosque-set Salah and iqamah timetables, Azan notifications, Qibla, Hijri calendar, mosque search and donation options, with admins able to manage Iqama, Ramadan and Eid schedules.
competitors.pricing: App listing states '100% Free and without any Ads, no subscription needed'.
competitors.overlap: Prayer times, congregation app notifications, some donation options.
competitors.gap_vs_masjidone: Madrasah management, branded website and Gift Aid are not mentioned on the pages fetched. (Mosque display screens were referenced in search snippets but not confirmed on a fetched page.) Free pricing makes it a strong substitute for the prayer-times part.

competitors.name: easyDonate
competitors.what_they_offer: UK donation platform for charities and organisations: in-person donation kiosks, online donations and Gift Aid (Standard and Small Donations Scheme) with HMRC-ready reports.
competitors.pricing: No figures published on the homepage; it states 'We don't work on any percentages or commission, you keep all the donations you make.'
competitors.overlap: Donations with no commission and Gift Aid.
competitors.gap_vs_masjidone: Madrasah management, prayer times, congregation app, website and screens are not mentioned on the page fetched; it is not mosque-specific.

positioning_takeaways: On the pages fetched, no competitor appeared to combine madrasah management (registers, fees, parent access) with congregation tools; madrasah tools (IBEAMS, Teach 'n Go) and congregation tools (Masjidbox, MosqueApp, MAWAQIT) appear to sit in separate products — this supports the 'one system / one family record' message, but must be re-verified before any comparative claim.

'0% commission and Gift Aid' is unlikely to be a differentiator on its own: Masjidbox advertises a 0% platform fee and automatic UK Gift Aid claiming, and easyDonate says it takes no commission. Lead with integration, not fee.

Price anchors are low on single-purpose tools: IBEAMS starts at £15/month with no set-up fee, Masjidbox has free tiers, MAWAQIT is free. MasjidOne's £499 setup fee will need justifying by the joined-up madrasah + congregation value and direct UK support.

MosqueApp Ltd is the closest UK-based like-for-like on the congregation side and lists a madrasah module as a future feature — MasjidOne's window to claim 'built madrasah portal' is real but may narrow; also avoid promoting parent access as done until its status is confirmed.

Support model may differentiate: IBEAMS charges £10/month for phone support, whereas MasjidOne's profile states masājid speak directly to the team who wrote the system — usable as a hedged, non-comparative claim about MasjidOne itself.
